headline: Pre-open setup: NVDA on 7-day losing streak into Wed earnings; futures rebound
summary: Nvidia closed Monday at $208.48 (-2.91%), its 7th straight down day and longest losing streak since Sept 2022 (~7% drawdown vs. S&P -1.2%). Buy-side whisper is $95-98B revenue vs. Street $92-95B and company guide $91B ±2%; focus is Q3 guide and the Blackwell→Vera Rubin transition. S&P e-minis +0.38% and Nasdaq-100 +0.85% pre-market Tuesday as chip names recover: AMD and MU +3%, INTC +2%. Straddle implies a ~7% post-print move Wednesday; a soft datacenter print would reset AI-capex sentiment given rich positioning.

headline: Stifel raises Micron PT to $173 (from $145), reiterates Buy ahead of print
summary: Stifel's Brian Chin raised his MU price target to $173 from $145 and kept a Buy rating going into Micron's fiscal Q4 report. Thesis rests on DRAM/NAND ASP acceleration, HBM3E ramp into NVDA/AMD, and Micron closing the HBM4 qualification gap with SK Hynix / Samsung. PT sits above the Street median ($155) and reinforces the memory-cycle bull case shared by 000660.KS and 005930.KS.

headline: Bernstein double-upgrades ASML to Outperform; names it top 2026 European semi pick
summary: Bernstein upgraded ASML to Outperform and named it its top pick among European semiconductor stocks for 2026, pointing to (1) accelerating memory-tool investment as SK Hynix / Samsung / Micron chase HBM4 capacity, (2) firmer logic demand from TSM's N2/A16 ramp, and (3) a more supportive valuation after the mid-summer semi selloff. Read-throughs: bullish for KLAC/LRCX/AMAT and 8035.T; supports Lam's constructive commentary that 2026 WFE tracks toward ~$150B vs. prior $140B guide.

headline: Energy Vault signs 1.25 GW off-grid hyperscaler power deal in Texas; $500-600M rev impact
summary: Energy Vault announced a strategic agreement with a leading power-generation EPC to deploy 1.25 GW of integrated off-grid power infrastructure — battery energy storage, grid-forming power conversion, and AI infrastructure control software — paired with Caterpillar gensets at a hyperscale AI datacenter development in Texas. Company guides $500-600M revenue impact across 2H 2026 and 2027. Notable as another example of hyperscalers bypassing utility interconnection queues in ERCOT; incrementally supportive for gas-turbine and battery-integrated names (GEV, ETN, FLNC) and read-through for TX capacity constraints affecting VST / NRG.

headline: NRG in advanced talks on 1.2 GW gas plant for unnamed hyperscaler amid Texas datacenter pause
summary: NRG Energy said it is 'aligned on principal commercial terms' with an unnamed 'global cloud and AI hyperscaler' for the development of a 1.2 GW combined-cycle natural-gas plant in Texas. Deal comes as ERCOT weighs a temporary pause on new large-load datacenter interconnections. Directly bullish for GEV / Siemens Energy gas-turbine backlog and reinforces the thesis that behind-the-meter and dedicated-gas solutions are now the fastest path to power for Tier-1 AI operators. Supportive for VST (existing TX gas fleet re-rates on scarcity value).

headline: Digital Realty and Equinix both raise FY outlooks as datacenter leasing and pricing accelerate
summary: Both DLR and EQIX raised full-year guidance in early-August updates, citing accelerating leasing volume and pricing power for retail-colo and hyperscale wholesale space. DLR flagged $500M+ of new bookings dominated by >1 MW deployments; EQIX pointed to AI-driven interconnection revenue growth. Confirms the mid-cycle read that datacenter REITs are seeing power-constrained supply push effective rents higher; supportive for CRWV bond demand (Goldman testing $1.15B CoreWeave-tied datacenter bond, Aug 19) and re-rates DLR/EQIX multiples versus broader REIT complex.

headline: Goldman double-downgrades Texas Instruments and Arm Holdings to Sell; sees them missing next AI leg
summary: Goldman Sachs cut Texas Instruments (TXN) and Arm Holdings (ARM) to Sell, arguing neither is well-positioned for the next phase of the semiconductor upcycle despite a constructive AI-spend backdrop into 2027. Analog/auto exposure at TXN and Arm's royalty mix are called out as insufficient betas to AI-datacenter capex; Goldman prefers NVDA, AVGO, TSM, and memory (MU / 000660.KS) as vehicles. Not a tracked-ticker action but a directional read: capital continues to concentrate in the AI-accelerator + HBM + WFE trio.

headline: Alibaba Q1 print reframes Chinese AI capex — 45% cloud growth, AI revenue run-rate ~$7.3B
summary: Follow-through from BABA's Aug 20 print: Alibaba Cloud external revenue accelerated to +45% YoY with AI-related product revenue in triple-digit growth for the 12th straight quarter. AI now 35% of Cloud external revenue at ~RMB 49.5B (~$7.3B) annualized. Capex surged 75% YoY (why the stock sold off 7%), but the datapoint reinforces that Chinese hyperscalers are matching US capex intensity — bullish for TSM (n-2 China cloud silicon), incremental positive for HBM demand (000660.KS, MU) via non-US routes still available under the current chip-export regime.

headline: Intuit reports fiscal Q4 tonight AMC; consumption-based AI pricing rollout in focus
summary: INTU reports fiscal Q4 (F26) after the close. Company guide: revenue +11-12% YoY, adj. EPS $3.56-$3.62; FY26 revenue $21.34-21.37B (+13-14%), adj. EPS $23.80-23.85 (+~18%). CEO Sasan Goodarzi has flagged an August rollout of an AI-driven expert platform on consumption-based pricing — key watch item for gross-margin trajectory and whether AI monetization can offset SMB/TurboTax cyclicality. Polymarket implies 94% odds of a beat. Not a direct tracked ticker but a bellwether for AI monetization in enterprise software (PLTR / CRM / NOW / SNOW read-through).

headline: Nvidia signals >15% price hike on Vera Rubin + Blackwell servers shipping early 2027
summary: Bloomberg reports Nvidia has notified server-OEM customers that systems built on Vera Rubin and Blackwell chips will carry price increases of more than 15%, effective on units shipping in early 2027. Move underscores pricing power heading into the next-gen ramp and is directly ASP-supportive for SMCI, DELL, HPE, and CLS builds; also positive for TSM (CoWoS-L attach) and HBM suppliers (000660.KS, MU, 005930.KS) that share in per-system BOM growth. Watch for framing on the Q2 call Wednesday.
